Harmonized Drug Dataset Quality Control

James Bannon, Michael Tran

September 28, 2026

1 Overview

This report is a quality control walkthrough for the lab-generated Harmonized Drug Dataset stored as a MultiAssayExperiment (MAE). The dataset harmonizes multiple drug-related assays and features across a shared compound universe keyed by HDD.Compound.ID so downstream analyses can operate on a consistent sample space. Pubchem.CID is retained when available, but it is not required for a compound to be included. The report resolves the release identity and expected dimensions from config/pipeline.yaml and the object’s embedded pipeline metadata, so the same checks remain useful for later regenerations.

1.1 Data Sources

The MAE is constructed in workflow/scripts/construct_MAE.R. This report inspects the released MAE and its exported tables. Key sources (from config/pipeline.yaml and the workflow scripts) include:

  • DeepChem datasets (Tox21 and SIDER): downloaded from DeepChem S3 and matched locally to HDD identities. Exact SMILES are considered first, then a full RDKit InChIKey is derived locally when no exact match exists. A single HDD candidate is accepted; a multi-candidate match is accepted only when exactly one candidate is an AnnotationDB compound. Other ambiguous and unmatched rows are dropped. No PubChem API or downloaded SMILES-to-CID table is used for this matching.
  • JUMP-CP membership and source identifiers from the curated cpg0016 MAE.
  • OASIS membership and source identifiers from the curated cpg0037 MAE.
  • GEOM membership and source identifiers from the curated GEOM MAE.
  • LINCS membership and source identifiers from the curated LINCS MAE.
  • CTRPv2 membership and master compound identifiers from the CTRPv2 PharmacoSet.
  • NCI60 membership and NSC identifiers from the NCI60-2026 PharmacoSet.
  • Bioassays: pulled from AnnotationDB alongside compound metadata, with bioassays filtered to gold-standard assays.
  • Drug indications: ChEMBL indication records pulled from AnnotationDB and stored as a long table in MAE metadata rather than flattened into colData.
  • ATC codes: pulled from AnnotationDB when an authorization key is available.
  • LTKB: DILI labels pulled from AnnotationDB for the LTKB Benchmark Dataset, DILIrank, and DILIst label sets.
  • LiverTox: hepatotoxicity likelihood score and reason pulled from AnnotationDB.
  • DIRIL and DICT: renal and cardiac toxicity labels pulled from AnnotationDB.
  • Fingerprints: RDKit Morgan count fingerprints generated for compounds with parseable SMILES.

suppressPackageStartupMessages({

})

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

if (!file.exists(config_path)) {

}

hdd_path <- file.path(results_dir, paste0(dataset_id, ".RDS"))

}
hdd_mae <- readRDS(hdd_path)
hdd_mae

2.1 Release identity and source provenance

The object embeds its release identity, the complete pipeline configuration, and the AnnotationDB response provenance used to construct the compound universe. These checks protect against rendering a report against a stale or misnamed object.

object_metadata <- S4Vectors::metadata(hdd_mae)
pipeline_metadata <- object_metadata$Pipeline

release_identity <- tibble::tibble(
  field = c(
    "Dataset ID",
    "Version",
    "AnnotationDB endpoint",
    "AnnotationDB fetched at (UTC)",
    "AnnotationDB record count",
    "AnnotationDB JSONL SHA-256"
  ),
  value = as.character(c(
    pipeline_metadata$ID,
    pipeline_metadata$Version,
    pipeline_metadata$Source.API,
    pipeline_metadata$Source.Fetched.At.UTC,
    pipeline_metadata$Source.Record.Count,
    pipeline_metadata$Source.JSONL.SHA256
  ))
)

release_identity
stopifnot(
  identical(pipeline_metadata$ID, dataset_id),
  identical(pipeline_metadata$Version, dataset_version)
)
format_file_size <- function(bytes) {
  if (is.na(bytes)) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }

  units <- c("B", "KB", "MB", "GB")
  unit_idx <- 1
  value <- bytes
  while (value >= 1024 && unit_idx < length(units)) {
    value <- value / 1024
    unit_idx <- unit_idx + 1
  }

  sprintf("%.1f %s", value, units[[unit_idx]])
}

expected_outputs <- c(
  hdd_path,
  file.path(results_dir, paste0(dataset_id, "_tables")),
  file.path(results_dir, paste0(dataset_id, "_tables.tar.gz"))
)

output_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  path = expected_outputs,
  exists = file.exists(expected_outputs),
  size = vapply(
    expected_outputs,
    function(path) {
      if (file.exists(path) && !dir.exists(path)) {
        file.info(path)$size
      } else if (dir.exists(path)) {
        sum(
          file.info(list.files(path, recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE))$size,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
      } else {
        NA_real_
      }
    },
    numeric(1)
  ),
  size_pretty = vapply(size, format_file_size, character(1)),
  modified = as.POSIXct(
    vapply(
      expected_outputs,
      function(path) {
        if (file.exists(path)) {
          file.info(path)$mtime
        } else {
          NA
        }
      },
      as.POSIXct(NA)
    ),
    origin = "1970-01-01"
  )
)

output_summary

3 MAE snapshot

experiment_names <- names(experiments(hdd_mae))
experiment_names
## [1] "SIDER"                     "Bioassays"                
## [3] "Tox21"                     "fingerprint.Morgan.2.1024"
## [5] "fingerprint.Morgan.2.2048" "fingerprint.Morgan.3.1024"
## [7] "fingerprint.Morgan.3.2048"
has_experiment <- function(name) {
  name %in% experiment_names
}

assay_missing_fraction <- function(assay_obj) {
  dims <- dim(assay_obj)
  total_values <- prod(dims)

  if (inherits(assay_obj, "sparseMatrix")) {
    stored_values <- if ("x" %in% slotNames(assay_obj)) {
      slot(assay_obj, "x")
    } else {
      NULL
    }

    if (length(stored_values) == 0) {
      return(0)
    }
    return(sum(is.na(stored_values)) / total_values)
  }

  mean(is.na(assay_obj))
}

summarize_experiment <- function(se) {
  assay_obj <- assays(se)[[1]]
  data_class <- class(assay_obj)[1]
  dims <- dim(assay_obj)
  missing_fraction <- assay_missing_fraction(assay_obj)

  data.frame(
    assay_name = assayNames(se)[1],
    rows = dims[1],
    cols = dims[2],
    row_metadata_fields = ncol(rowData(se)),
    data_class = data_class,
    missing_fraction = missing_fraction,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

experiment_summary <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(experiments(hdd_mae), summarize_experiment)
)
rownames(experiment_summary) <- experiment_names
experiment_summary

3.1 Experiment schema and release gates

The current release contract contains SIDER, Bioassays, Tox21, and each Morgan fingerprint requested by configuration.

fingerprint_config <- config$colData$fingerprints
expected_fingerprints <- unlist(lapply(
  fingerprint_config$radius_list,
  function(radius) {
    paste0(
      "fingerprint.Morgan.",
      radius,
      ".",
      fingerprint_config$dim_list
    )
  }
))
expected_experiments <- c(
  "SIDER",
  "Bioassays",
  "Tox21",
  expected_fingerprints
)
object_validity <- validObject(hdd_mae, test = TRUE)
compound_ids <- as.character(colData(hdd_mae)$HDD.Compound.ID)

experiment_schema_checks <- tibble::tibble(
  check = c(
    "MAE passes validObject",
    "HDD compound IDs are present and unique",
    "HDD compound IDs equal colData row names",
    "Experiment set matches the release contract"
  ),
  passed = c(
    identical(object_validity, TRUE),
    !any(is.na(compound_ids)) && anyDuplicated(compound_ids) == 0L,
    identical(rownames(colData(hdd_mae)), compound_ids),
    setequal(experiment_names, expected_experiments)
  ),
  detail = c(
    if (identical(object_validity, TRUE)) {
      "validObject returned TRUE"
    } else {
      paste(object_validity, collapse = "; ")
    },
    paste(scales::comma(length(compound_ids)), "compound IDs"),
    "colData row names use HDD.Compound.ID",
    paste(experiment_names, collapse = ", ")
  )
)

experiment_schema_checks
stopifnot(all(experiment_schema_checks$passed))

source_key_coverage <- tibble::tribble(
  ~source, ~flag_column, ~key_column,
  "LINCS", "In.LINCS", "LINCS.CMap.Name",
  "JUMP-CP", "In.JUMP.CP", "JUMP.CP.ID",
  "OASIS", "In.OASIS", "OASIS.ID",
  "GEOM", "In.GEOM", "GEOM.Source.SMILES",
  "CTRPv2", "In.CTRP", "CTRP.Master.CPD.ID",
  "NCI60", "In.NCI60", "NCI60.NSC"
) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    member_compounds = sum(
      as.logical(colData(hdd_mae)[[flag_column]]),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    members_with_source_key = {
      member <- as.logical(colData(hdd_mae)[[flag_column]])
      key <- trimws(as.character(colData(hdd_mae)[[key_column]]))
      sum(member & !is.na(key) & key != "", na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    key_coverage = ifelse(
      member_compounds == 0L,
      NA_real_,
      members_with_source_key / member_compounds
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

source_key_coverage

4.1 Long-form drug indications

Drug indication records are one-to-many with compounds and therefore remain a long table in metadata(hdd_mae)$Drug.Indications. This avoids flattening or silently discarding repeated ChEMBL indications in colData. The foreign-key check below requires every indication row to point to a compound in the MAE.

drug_indications <- as.data.frame(object_metadata$Drug.Indications)
invalid_indication_ids <- setdiff(
  drug_indications$HDD.Compound.ID,
  cd$HDD.Compound.ID
)

indication_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  indication_rows = nrow(drug_indications),
  compounds_with_indications = dplyr::n_distinct(
    drug_indications$HDD.Compound.ID
  ),
  unique_chembl_indications = dplyr::n_distinct(
    drug_indications$ChEMBL.Drug.Indication.ID,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ),
  invalid_compound_foreign_keys = length(invalid_indication_ids)
)

indication_summary
head(drug_indications, 10)
stopifnot(
  nrow(drug_indications) == config$dataset$expected_indication_count,
  !any(is.na(drug_indications$HDD.Compound.ID)),
  length(invalid_indication_ids) == 0L
)

4.1.1 Clinical annotation coverage and ontology mappings

These annotations describe compound–indication associations, not a single clinical status assigned to each compound. MeSH identifiers and headings are retained alongside the source’s EFO.ID and EFO.Term fields. Despite that field name, the identifiers can belong to EFO, MONDO, HP, or other namespaces; the table below reports the prefixes actually present rather than assuming every mapping is an EFO identifier. Counts of records, compounds, and source indications are distinct: a source indication can occur for multiple HDD IDs.

has_annotation <- function(x) {
  !is.na(x) & nzchar(trimws(as.character(x)))
}
clinical_fields <- c(
  "MeSH.ID", "MeSH.Heading", "EFO.ID", "EFO.Term",
  "Maximum.Indication.Phase", "Clinical.Trial.Reference.IDs",
  "DailyMed.Reference.IDs", "EMA.Reference.IDs", "FDA.Reference.IDs"
)
clinical_coverage <- bind_rows(lapply(clinical_fields, function(field) {
  present <- has_annotation(drug_indications[[field]])
  tibble::tibble(
    Field = field,
    Records = sum(present),
    `Percent of indication records` = round(100 * mean(present), 1),
    `Distinct HDD compounds` = n_distinct(drug_indications$HDD.Compound.ID[present])
  )
}))
knitr::kable(clinical_coverage)

ontology_coverage <- drug_indications |>
  filter(has_annotation(EFO.ID)) |>
  mutate(Namespace = sub("[:_].*$", "", EFO.ID)) |>
  group_by(Namespace) |>
  summarise(
    Records = n(),
    `Distinct identifiers` = n_distinct(EFO.ID),
    `Distinct HDD compounds` = n_distinct(HDD.Compound.ID),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(Records))

4.1.2 Indication-specific development phases

The distribution below uses Maximum.Indication.Phase exactly as supplied by AnnotationDB/ChEMBL, including fractional and negative source codes. It is the maximum phase recorded for the particular indication, not necessarily an active trial’s phase or the compound’s overall development status. No source codes are relabeled as regulatory approval claims. Bars count association records; a compound with several indications can contribute more than once.

indication_phases <- drug_indications |>
  group_by(Maximum.Indication.Phase) |>
  summarise(
    Records = n(),
    Compounds = n_distinct(HDD.Compound.ID),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(Maximum.Indication.Phase)
stopifnot(sum(indication_phases$Records) == nrow(drug_indications))
knitr::kable(indication_phases)
Maximum.Indication.Phase Records Compounds
-1.0 129 117
0.5 1210 750
1.0 9676 2308
2.0 18932 3198
3.0 15946 2456
4.0 9613 2703 
ggplot(indication_phases, aes(
  x = factor(Maximum.Indication.Phase, levels = indication_phases$Maximum.Indication.Phase),
  y = Records
)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2C7FB8") +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(Records)), vjust = -0.35) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = "Maximum indication phase (source code)", y = "Compound–indication records") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

4.1.3 Examples of curated indication records

One example per observed phase illustrates the retained disease names, ontology mappings, and compound identifiers. These are deterministic examples from the final object, not a claim of efficacy or current treatment guidance. Parent/child inference flags and supporting reference identifiers remain in the full table for provenance; inferred associations are not discarded here.

indication_examples <- drug_indications |>
  arrange(Maximum.Indication.Phase, HDD.Compound.ID, ChEMBL.Drug.Indication.ID, EFO.ID) |>
  group_by(Maximum.Indication.Phase) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(compound_labels, by = c("HDD.Compound.ID" = "sample_id")) |>
  select(
    Compound = compound_label, HDD.Compound.ID, Maximum.Indication.Phase,
    MeSH.ID, MeSH.Heading, EFO.ID, EFO.Term
  )
knitr::kable(indication_examples)

  count(Inferred.From.Parent, Inferred.From.Child, name = "Records") |>

The same records are available in the release’s metadata/drug_indications.tsv export. The check below compares the complete export against the object without querying external services.

indication_export <- readr::read_tsv(
  file.path(table_dir, "metadata", "drug_indications.tsv"),
  col_types = readr::cols(
    .default = readr::col_character(),
    Pubchem.CID = readr::col_double(),
    ChEMBL.Drug.Indication.ID = readr::col_double(),
    Maximum.Indication.Phase = readr::col_double(),
    Inferred.From.Parent = readr::col_logical(),
    Inferred.From.Child = readr::col_logical()
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
stopifnot(
  nrow(readr::problems(indication_export)) == 0L,
  identical(names(indication_export), names(drug_indications)),
  nrow(indication_export) == nrow(drug_indications)
)
indication_export_checks <- tibble::tibble(
  Field = names(drug_indications),
  Matches = vapply(names(drug_indications), function(field) {
    identical(as.character(indication_export[[field]]), as.character(drug_indications[[field]]))
  }, logical(1))
)

5 Experiment walkthroughs

Below, each experiment in the HDD MAE is reviewed.

5.1 Bioassays

A compound-by-assay matrix of PubChem bioassay outcomes. Rows are AIDs (assay identifiers) and columns are HDD.Compound.ID values. Entries are categorical outcomes, with missing values representing compounds that were not measured.

se <- experiments(hdd_mae)[["Bioassays"]]
assay_mat <- assay(se)

c(rows = nrow(assay_mat), cols = ncol(assay_mat))
##   rows   cols 
##     33 438498
assay_mat[1:min(5, nrow(assay_mat)), 1:min(6, ncol(assay_mat))]
# Category counts
assay_mat_chr <- as.matrix(assay_mat)
assay_values <- ifelse(
  is.na(assay_mat_chr),
  "Not Measured",
  as.character(assay_mat_chr)
)
category_counts <- sort(table(assay_values), decreasing = TRUE)
category_counts
## assay_values
## Not Measured       Active 
##     13892790       577644
inactive_count <- if ("Inactive" %in% names(category_counts)) {
  category_counts[["Inactive"]]
} else {
  0
}
cat("Inactive values in current Bioassays matrix:", inactive_count, "\n")
## Inactive values in current Bioassays matrix: 0
# Missingness proxy: Not Measured rate per assay
not_measured_rate <- rowMeans(is.na(assay_mat_chr))
summary(not_measured_rate)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##   0.872   0.948   0.988   0.960   0.989   1.000
bio_counts <- tibble::tibble(
  status = factor(
    names(category_counts),
    levels = c("Active", "Inactive", "Not Measured")
  ),
  count = as.numeric(category_counts)
)

bio_by_assay <- t(apply(assay_mat_chr, 1, function(values) {
  table(factor(
    ifelse(is.na(values), "Not Measured", as.character(values)),
    levels = c("Active", "Inactive", "Not Measured")
  ))
})) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("assay") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-assay, names_to = "status", values_to = "count")

bio_by_assay$status <- factor(
  bio_by_assay$status,
  levels = c("Active", "Inactive", "Not Measured")
)

ggplot(bio_counts, aes(x = status, y = count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4C78A8") +
  labs(
    title = "Bioassays overall category counts",
    x = "Outcome",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(bio_by_assay, aes(x = assay, y = count, fill = status)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Bioassays outcome composition by assay",
    x = "Assay (AID)",
    y = "Fraction",
    fill = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

5.2 Tox21

A compound-by-assay matrix for the Tox21 panel. Rows are Tox21 assays and columns are HDD.Compound.ID values. Values are typically binary (0/1) with missing values for unmeasured compounds.

se <- experiments(hdd_mae)[["Tox21"]]
assay_mat <- assay(se)

c(rows = nrow(assay_mat), cols = ncol(assay_mat))
## rows cols 
##   12 5867
assay_mat[1:min(5, nrow(assay_mat)), 1:min(6, ncol(assay_mat))]
# Value distribution
assay_mat_num <- as.matrix(assay_mat)
if ("mol_id" %in% rownames(assay_mat_num)) {
  assay_mat_num <- assay_mat_num[
    rownames(assay_mat_num) != "mol_id",
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
}
table(as.vector(assay_mat_num), useNA = "ifany")
## 
##     0     1  <NA> 
## 53926  4597 11881
# Missingness per assay
summary(rowMeans(is.na(assay_mat_num)))
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##  0.0721  0.1286  0.1646  0.1688  0.2176  0.2630
tox21_long <- as.data.frame(assay_mat_num) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("assay") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-assay, names_to = "compound", values_to = "value")
tox21_long$value_factor <- factor(tox21_long$value, levels = c(0, 1))

tox21_compound_summary <- tox21_long |>
  group_by(compound) |>
  summarize(positive_count = sum(value == 1, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(compound_labels, by = c("compound" = "sample_id")) |>
  arrange(positive_count, compound)

tox21_plot_compounds <- bind_rows(
  tox21_compound_summary |> slice_head(n = 20) |> mutate(group = "Bottom 20"),
  tox21_compound_summary |> slice_tail(n = 20) |> mutate(group = "Top 20")
) |>
  distinct(compound, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(positive_count, compound)

tox21_plot <- tox21_long |>
  filter(compound %in% tox21_plot_compounds$compound) |>
  left_join(
    tox21_plot_compounds |>
      select(compound, compound_label),
    by = "compound"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    compound_label = factor(
      compound_label,
      levels = tox21_plot_compounds$compound_label
    )
  )

ggplot(tox21_plot, aes(x = compound_label, y = assay, fill = value_factor)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("0" = "#d1d5db", "1" = "#2563eb"),
    na.value = "#f3f4f6"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Tox21 outcomes (0/1) for compounds with the lowest and highest positive counts",
    x = "Drug name",
    y = "Assay",
    fill = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))

tox21_rate <- tox21_long |>
  group_by(assay) |>
  summarize(positive_rate = mean(value == 1, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(tox21_rate, aes(x = reorder(assay, positive_rate), y = positive_rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4C78A8") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Tox21 positive rate by assay",
    x = "Assay",
    y = "Positive rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

5.3 Tox21 and SIDER release dimensions

The final assays are checked against the configured release dimensions.

deepchem_experiment_names <- c(tox21 = "Tox21", sider = "SIDER")
deepchem_dimension_checks <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(
  names(deepchem_experiment_names),
  function(dataset_key) {
    experiment_name <- deepchem_experiment_names[[dataset_key]]
    observed <- dim(experiments(hdd_mae)[[experiment_name]])
    expected <- config$deep_chem$expected_assays[[dataset_key]]

    tibble::tibble(
      dataset = experiment_name,
      observed_features = observed[[1]],
      expected_features = expected$features,
      observed_compounds = observed[[2]],
      expected_compounds = expected$compounds,
      passed = observed[[1]] == expected$features &&
        observed[[2]] == expected$compounds
    )
  }
))

deepchem_dimension_checks
stopifnot(all(deepchem_dimension_checks$passed))

5.4 SIDER

A compound-by-side-effect matrix derived from SIDER. Rows are side effect categories and columns are HDD.Compound.ID values. Values are binary (0/1) with missing values when a compound is not represented.

se <- experiments(hdd_mae)[["SIDER"]]
assay_mat <- assay(se)

c(rows = nrow(assay_mat), cols = ncol(assay_mat))
## rows cols 
##   27 1397
assay_mat[1:min(5, nrow(assay_mat)), 1:min(6, ncol(assay_mat))]

## Metabolism and nutrition disorders                1                1
## Product issues                                    0                0
## Eye disorders                                     0                0
## Investigations                                    1                1
##                                    HDD_bn4qZQZNf8lw HDD_PDmrpvRaQUTU
## Hepatobiliary disorders                           0                1
## Metabolism and nutrition disorders                1                1
## Product issues                                    0                0
## Eye disorders                                     1                1
## Investigations                                    1                1
##                                    HDD_rOPijtNimrd1 HDD_MwdiJlr9ygRr
## Hepatobiliary disorders                           1                0
## Metabolism and nutrition disorders                1                1
## Product issues                                    0                0
## Eye disorders                                     1                1
## Investigations                                    1                1
# Value distribution
assay_mat_num <- as.matrix(assay_mat)
table(as.vector(assay_mat_num), useNA = "ifany")
## 
##     0     1 
## 16347 21372
# Missingness per side effect
summary(rowMeans(is.na(assay_mat_num)))
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##       0       0       0       0       0       0
sider_counts <- as.data.frame(table(
  value = as.vector(assay_mat_num),
  useNA = "ifany"
))

ggplot(sider_counts, aes(x = value, y = Freq)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4C78A8") +
  labs(
    title = "SIDER value counts",
    x = "Value",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

row_non_missing <- rowSums(!is.na(assay_mat_num))
row_positive <- rowSums(assay_mat_num == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
row_rate <- row_positive / row_non_missing

sider_effects <- tibble::tibble(
  side_effect = rownames(assay_mat_num),
  positive_rate = as.numeric(row_rate)
)

ggplot(
  sider_effects,
  aes(x = reorder(side_effect, positive_rate), y = positive_rate)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "#72B7B2") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "SIDER positive rate by side effect",
    x = "Side effect",
    y = "Positive rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

col_non_missing <- colSums(!is.na(assay_mat_num))
col_positive <- colSums(assay_mat_num == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
col_rate <- col_positive / col_non_missing

ggplot(tibble::tibble(positive_rate = col_rate), aes(x = positive_rate)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 12, fill = "#3A6EA5", alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "SIDER positive rate across compounds",
    x = "Positive rate",
    y = "Compound count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

5.5 Fingerprints (Morgan count fingerprints)

Count-based Morgan fingerprints generated from parseable SMILES using RDKit. Each fingerprint experiment is stored as a sparse matrix of feature counts with rows as fingerprint bins and columns as the HDD.Compound.ID values that produced a fingerprint. Compounds with missing or invalid SMILES remain in colData but are not columns in the fingerprint experiments.

fp_names <- grep("^fingerprint\\.", experiment_names, value = TRUE)
fp_names
## [1] "fingerprint.Morgan.2.1024" "fingerprint.Morgan.2.2048"
## [3] "fingerprint.Morgan.3.1024" "fingerprint.Morgan.3.2048"
preferred_fp_names <- c(
  "fingerprint.Morgan.3.1024",
  "fingerprint.Morgan.3.2048",
  "fingerprint.Morgan.2.1024",
  "fingerprint.Morgan.2.2048"
)
selected_fp_name <- preferred_fp_names[preferred_fp_names %in% fp_names][1]
selected_fp_name
## [1] "fingerprint.Morgan.3.1024"
fingerprint_coverage <- tibble::tibble(
  total_compounds = nrow(cd),
  compounds_with_smiles = sum(!is.na(cd$SMILES)),
  selected_fingerprint_columns = if (is.na(selected_fp_name)) {
    NA_integer_
  } else {
    ncol(assay(experiments(hdd_mae)[[selected_fp_name]]))
  },
  not_fingerprinted = total_compounds - selected_fingerprint_columns
)

fingerprint_coverage
for (fp_name in fp_names) {
  se <- experiments(hdd_mae)[[fp_name]]
  assay_mat <- assays(se)[[1]]

  cat("\nFingerprint:", fp_name, "\n")
  cat("Dimensions:", nrow(assay_mat), "x", ncol(assay_mat), "\n")

  # Sparsity for sparse matrices
  if (inherits(assay_mat, "sparseMatrix")) {
    sparsity <- 1 - Matrix::nnzero(assay_mat) / length(assay_mat)
    cat("Sparsity:", round(sparsity, 4), "\n")
  }

  print(assay_mat[1:min(5, nrow(assay_mat)), 1:min(6, ncol(assay_mat))])
}

for (fp_name in fp_names) {
  se <- experiments(hdd_mae)[[fp_name]]
  assay_mat <- assays(se)[[1]]

  col_nnz <- Matrix::colSums(assay_mat > 0)
  row_nnz <- Matrix::rowSums(assay_mat > 0)

  nnz_df <- tibble::tibble(
    count = c(as.numeric(col_nnz), as.numeric(row_nnz)),
    axis = rep(c("Compound", "Feature"), c(length(col_nnz), length(row_nnz)))
  )

  p_nnz <- ggplot(nnz_df, aes(x = count, fill = axis)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    labs(
      title = paste("Fingerprint non-zero counts:", fp_name),
      x = "Non-zero features per entity",
      y = "Count",
      fill = ""
    ) +
    theme_minimal()

  nonzero_vals <- assay_mat@x
  val_df <- as.data.frame(table(value = nonzero_vals))

  p_vals <- ggplot(val_df, aes(x = value, y = Freq)) +
    geom_col(fill = "#3A6EA5") +
    labs(
      title = paste("Fingerprint count values:", fp_name),
      x = "Count value",
      y = "Frequency"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()

  print(p_nnz)
  print(p_vals)
}

5.6 ATC code coverage

AnnotationDB ATC data requires an authorization key. If the key is not set, the pipeline still builds the HDD with other AnnotationDB fields and leaves ATC.Code missing.

stopifnot("ATC.Code" %in% colnames(cd))

atc_values <- trimws(as.character(cd$ATC.Code))
atc_coverage <- tibble::tibble(
  status = c("ATC code present", "ATC code missing"),
  compounds = c(
    sum(!is.na(atc_values) & atc_values != ""),
    sum(is.na(atc_values) | atc_values == "")
  )
)

ggplot(atc_coverage, aes(x = status, y = compounds, fill = status)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(compounds)), vjust = -0.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::comma,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "ATC code present" = "#26734D",
    "ATC code missing" = "#BDBDBD"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "ATC code coverage in HDD compound metadata",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Compounds"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

5.7 DILI, DIRIL, and DICT coverage

This section summarizes the toxicity metadata currently available in colData for liver, renal, and cardiac toxicity labels.

col.Data <- colData(hdd_mae) |>
  as.data.frame()

source_toxicity_columns <- tibble::tribble(
  ~source, ~label_set, ~field, ~column,
  "LTKB", "LTKB Benchmark Dataset", "DILI severity grade",
  "LTKB.DILI.Severity.Grade",
  "LTKB", "LTKB Benchmark Dataset", "DILI annotation", "LTKB.DILI.Annotation",
  "LTKB", "DILIrank", "DILI severity grade", "DILIrank.DILI.Severity.Grade",
  "LTKB", "DILIrank", "DILI annotation", "DILIrank.DILI.Annotation",
  "LTKB", "DILIst", "DILI annotation", "DILIst.DILI.Annotation",
  "LiverTox", "LiverTox", "hepatotoxicity likelihood score",
  "Livertox.Hepatotoxicity.Likelihood.Score",
  "LiverTox", "LiverTox", "hepatotoxicity likelihood reason",
  "Livertox.Hepatotoxicity.Likelihood.Reason"
)

diril_dict_columns <- tibble::tribble(
  ~source, ~field, ~column,
  "DIRIL", "Gong label", "DIRIL.Label.Gong",
  "DIRIL", "Shi label", "DIRIL.Label.Shi",
  "DIRIL", "final toxicity label", "DIRIL.Toxicity",
  "DICT", "cardiotoxicity class", "DICT.Cardiotoxicity",
  "DICT", "label section", "DICT.Label.Section",
  "DICT", "concern", "DICT.Concern",
  "DICT", "keywords", "DICT.Keywords"
)

count_non_missing <- function(column) {
  values <- as.character(col.Data[[column]])
  sum(!is.na(values) & trimws(values) != "")
}

count_unique_non_missing <- function(column) {
  values <- as.character(col.Data[[column]])
  non_missing_values <- values[!is.na(values) & trimws(values) != ""]
  length(unique(non_missing_values))
}

source_toxicity_coverage <- source_toxicity_columns |>
  mutate(
    non_missing = vapply(column, count_non_missing, integer(1)),
    unique_non_missing = vapply(column, count_unique_non_missing, integer(1))
  )

source_toxicity_coverage |>
  select(source, label_set, field, non_missing, unique_non_missing)
ggplot(
  source_toxicity_coverage |>
    mutate(label = paste(label_set, field, sep = ": ")),
  aes(x = reorder(label, non_missing), y = non_missing, fill = source)
) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Non-missing LTKB and LiverTox metadata",
    x = "Label set and field",
    y = "Non-missing compound count",
    fill = "Source"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

toxicity_label_count_columns <- bind_rows(
  source_toxicity_columns |>
    filter(field != "hepatotoxicity likelihood reason"),
  diril_dict_columns |>
    filter(field != "keywords")
)

toxicity_label_counts <- lapply(
  seq_len(nrow(toxicity_label_count_columns)),
  function(idx) {
    spec <- toxicity_label_count_columns[idx, ]
    values <- trimws(as.character(col.Data[[spec$column]]))

    tibble::tibble(
      source = spec$source,
      label_set = spec$label_set,
      field = spec$field,
      label = values
    ) |>
      filter(!is.na(label), label != "") |>
      count(source, label_set, field, label, sort = TRUE)
  }
) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

toxicity_label_counts
source_dili_severity_columns <- source_toxicity_columns |>
  filter(field == "DILI severity grade") |>
  pull(column)

dili_counts <- lapply(source_dili_severity_columns, function(column) {
  label_set_name <- source_toxicity_columns$label_set[
    match(column, source_toxicity_columns$column)
  ]

  tibble::tibble(
    label_set = label_set_name,
    column = column,
    severity_grade = trimws(as.character(col.Data[[column]]))
  ) |>
    filter(!is.na(severity_grade), severity_grade != "") |>
    count(label_set, column, severity_grade, sort = TRUE)
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  mutate(
    severity_grade = factor(
      severity_grade,
      levels = sort(unique(as.numeric(severity_grade)))
    )
  )

dili_counts
ggplot(dili_counts, aes(x = severity_grade, y = n, fill = label_set)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.72) +
  labs(
    title = "DILI severity annotation counts",
    x = "DILI severity grade",
    y = "Compound count",
    fill = "Label set"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

dili_severity_consensus <- col.Data |>
  transmute(
    LTKB = suppressWarnings(
      as.integer(trimws(as.character(LTKB.DILI.Severity.Grade)))
    ),
    DILIrank = suppressWarnings(
      as.integer(trimws(as.character(DILIrank.DILI.Severity.Grade)))
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(LTKB), !is.na(DILIrank)) |>
  count(LTKB, DILIrank, name = "n") |>
  tidyr::complete(
    LTKB = seq(min(LTKB), max(LTKB)),
    DILIrank = seq(min(DILIrank), max(DILIrank)),
    fill = list(n = 0L)
  )

ggplot(dili_severity_consensus, aes(x = LTKB, y = DILIrank, fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(n > 0, n, "")), size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(dili_severity_consensus$LTKB))) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(dili_severity_consensus$DILIrank))) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#EDF5FA", high = "#2F5D7C") +
  labs(
    title = "LTKB Benchmark Dataset and DILIrank severity grade agreement",
    x = "LTKB Benchmark Dataset severity grade",
    y = "DILIrank severity grade",
    fill = "Compound count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

diril_dict_coverage <- diril_dict_columns |>
  mutate(
    non_missing = vapply(column, count_non_missing, integer(1)),
    unique_non_missing = vapply(column, count_unique_non_missing, integer(1))
  )

diril_dict_coverage
moa_toxicity_label_columns <- tibble::tribble(
  ~source, ~label_set, ~field, ~column,
  "LTKB", "LTKB Benchmark Dataset", "DILI annotation", "LTKB.DILI.Annotation",
  "LTKB", "DILIrank", "DILI annotation", "DILIrank.DILI.Annotation",
  "LTKB", "DILIst", "DILI annotation", "DILIst.DILI.Annotation",
  "LiverTox", "LiverTox", "hepatotoxicity likelihood score",
  "Livertox.Hepatotoxicity.Likelihood.Score",
  "DIRIL", "DIRIL", "final toxicity label", "DIRIL.Toxicity",
  "DICT", "DICT", "concern", "DICT.Concern"
)

moa_toxicity_labels <- lapply(
  seq_len(nrow(moa_toxicity_label_columns)),
  function(idx) {
    spec <- moa_toxicity_label_columns[idx, ]
    moa <- trimws(as.character(col.Data$Mechanism.of.Action))
    label <- trimws(as.character(col.Data[[spec$column]]))

    tibble::tibble(
      source = spec$source,
      label_set = spec$label_set,
      field = spec$field,
      moa = moa,
      toxicity_label = label
    ) |>
      filter(
        !is.na(moa),
        moa != "",
        !is.na(toxicity_label),
        toxicity_label != ""
      )
  }
) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

wrap_plot_label <- function(value, width = 34) {
  vapply(
    value,
    function(item) {
      item <- trimws(as.character(item))
      if (is.na(item) || item == "") {
        return(NA_character_)
      }
      paste(strwrap(item, width = width), collapse = "\n")
    },
    character(1),
    USE.NAMES = FALSE
  )
}

moa_toxicity_counts <- moa_toxicity_labels |>
  count(source, label_set, field, moa, toxicity_label, sort = TRUE)

n_top_moa_toxicity_pairs <- 6

moa_toxicity_plot_data <- moa_toxicity_counts |>
  arrange(source, label_set, desc(n), moa, toxicity_label) |>
  group_by(source, label_set) |>
  slice_head(n = n_top_moa_toxicity_pairs) |>
  mutate(
    pair_rank = row_number(),
    pair_label = wrap_plot_label(moa, 42),
    toxicity_label_plot = wrap_plot_label(toxicity_label, 28),
    panel = paste(source, label_set, sep = ": "),
    pair_key = paste(panel, pair_rank, pair_label, sep = "|||")
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(source, label_set, desc(pair_rank)) |>
  mutate(
    source = factor(source, levels = unique(moa_toxicity_label_columns$source)),
    panel = factor(panel, levels = unique(panel)),
    pair_key = factor(pair_key, levels = unique(pair_key)),
    toxicity_label_plot = factor(
      toxicity_label_plot,
      levels = sort(unique(toxicity_label_plot))
    )
  )

toxicity_label_palette <- setNames(
  grDevices::hcl.colors(
    n = length(levels(moa_toxicity_plot_data$toxicity_label_plot)),
    palette = "Dark 3"
  ),
  levels(moa_toxicity_plot_data$toxicity_label_plot)
)

ggplot(
  moa_toxicity_plot_data,
  aes(x = n, y = pair_key, fill = toxicity_label_plot)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.15, size = 2.8) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = toxicity_label_palette) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(value) sub("^.*\\|\\|\\|", "", value)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)) +
  labs(
    title = "Top ChEMBL mechanism-of-action and toxicity-label combinations",
    x = "Compound count",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Toxicity label"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, lineheight = 0.95),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8, lineheight = 0.95),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(5.5, 28, 5.5, 5.5),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0)
  )

normalize_diril_label <- function(value) {
  value <- trimws(as.character(value))
  value[value == ""] <- NA_character_
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(value) ~ NA_character_,
    tolower(value) == "nephrotoxic" ~ "Nephrotoxic",
    tolower(value) == "non-nephrotoxic" ~ "Non-Nephrotoxic",
    TRUE ~ value
  )
}

diril_consensus <- col.Data |>
  transmute(
    Gong = normalize_diril_label(DIRIL.Label.Gong),
    Shi = normalize_diril_label(DIRIL.Label.Shi),
    Final = normalize_diril_label(DIRIL.Toxicity)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(Gong), !is.na(Shi), !is.na(Final)) |>
  count(Gong, Shi, Final, sort = TRUE)

diril_consensus
ggplot(diril_consensus, aes(x = Gong, y = Shi, fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~Final) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#D7E8F5", high = "#2F5D7C") +
  labs(
    title = "DIRIL Gong and Shi labels by final toxicity label",
    x = "Gong label",
    y = "Shi label",
    fill = "Compound count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

5.8 Basic access examples

The examples below show the intended access pattern for release metadata, compound annotations, one assay matrix, and a small analysis-ready table. They operate on the object already loaded by this report and do not query a live service.

compound_metadata_example <- as.data.frame(colData(hdd_mae)) |>
  select(
    HDD.Compound.ID,
    Molecule.Name,
    Pubchem.CID,
    ChEMBL.ID,
    In.AnnotationDB
  ) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)
compound_metadata_example
# One assay and a compact joined summary
tox21_matrix <- assay(experiments(hdd_mae)[["Tox21"]])
tox21_matrix[1:min(5, nrow(tox21_matrix)), 1:min(6, ncol(tox21_matrix))]
tox21_analysis_ready <- tibble::tibble(
  HDD.Compound.ID = colnames(tox21_matrix),
  measured_assays = colSums(!is.na(tox21_matrix)),
  positive_assays = colSums(tox21_matrix == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
) |>
  left_join(
    as.data.frame(colData(hdd_mae)) |>
      select(HDD.Compound.ID, Molecule.Name, Pubchem.CID),
    by = "HDD.Compound.ID"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(positive_assays), HDD.Compound.ID) |>
  slice_head(n = 20)
tox21_analysis_ready
